science.title: Blue Rings reveal thermal thresholds of wood formation in Low Arctic tundra shrubs
science.description: Low Arctic tundra shrubs experience short growing seasons, prolonged cool conditions, and episodic cold extremes, but the effects of these events on wood tissue formation remain poorly understood. Here we identify thermal thresholds associated with lignification processes in two dominant shrub taxa (Alnus alnobetula and Salix spp.) along a 68–69°N transect in northwestern Canada. Using wood anatomical indicators of incomplete secondary cell wall lignification (blue rings) and freezing-induced cell collapse (frost rings), we show that wood tissue development is sensitive to thermal stress at the beginning and end of the growing season. We identified thermal thresholds constraining shrub wood formation. Incomplete lignification resulting in blue rings was associated with cumulative August cold exposure below taxon-specific thresholds (~ 2 °C in Alnus, ~ 4 °C in Salix) and contrasting sensitivities to cumulative cold exposure. Early growing season frost injury in some cases followed prior-year incomplete lignification. The results indicate that contrasting forms of growing-season cold stress constrain distinct phases of wood formation and highlight taxon-specific thermal limits controlling shrub growth. By quantifying climatic controls on lignification failure and frost injury, we link sub-seasonal cold extremes to specific phases of wood formation, which may shape tundra vegetation responses under ongoing Arctic climate change.

science.title: Controlling the diffusion of fullerene-wheeled nanovehicles using hybrid curved substrates
science.description: In recent years, several types of nanocars have been developed, demonstrating significant capabilities in molecular transport, bottom-up assembly, and other mechanical tasks. This study proposes an approach for converting the diffusive movement of nanocars into guided motion by adding a gold impurity line to a silver cylindrical substrate in which the width of this gold line, depending on the angle of the arc facing it, varies between 120°, 150°, and 180° from the circumference of the complete cylinder; and the movement of C60, nanotruck, and nanocar on these substrates is investigated. The findings show that gold impurity acts as a repellent barrier, especially at 150°, effectively preventing C60 from entering the silver region even under high-temperature conditions, though the entry eventually occurred at 600 K. Nevertheless, a sufficiently large gold impurity acted as an impermeable obstacle for both the nanocar and nanotruck even at a high temperature of 600 K on 180° and 120°, respectively. The considered geometries effectively restricted deviations from the desired path. Furthermore, the effect of varying impurity line thickness is studied. The results reveal that adjusting the impurity line thickness leads to long-range motion and sufficient diffusion coefficient. The 150° and 180° substrates are optimal for C60 and nanocar across various temperatures, while the nanotruck performs best on the 120° substrate due to its rigid chassis. The presence of impurities within the substrate significantly limits the range of motion in nanomachines by acting as a repellent obstacle or snatching trap.

science.title: Placental TRPV2 supports trophoblast function and normal fetal development
science.description: While placental functioning arbitrates fetal outcome, the molecular players that underpin normal placental development remain poorly understood. Here, we provide evidence that the Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 2 (TRPV2) channel plays an important role in normal placental development, determining fetal size and survival. Its absence severely affects placental morphology, causing fetal growth restriction and embryonic lethality, which was found to be allocated to a non-redundant role in the trophoblast, but not in the embryo. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated Trpv2 deletion in mouse trophoblast stem cells demonstrated that Trpv2 contributes to the differentiation towards Syncytiotrophoblast layer II (SynTII) cells, which was confirmed by the growth restriction phenotype in SynTII-specific Trpv2 knockout animals. Finally, TRPV2 was functionally expressed in human trophoblast cells and enriched in trophoblast populations undergoing syncytial differentiation. Together, our findings identify an important role for TRPV2 during placental development and consequently fetal outcomes. Normal placental development is fundamental to fetal outcome, yet the molecular pathways that underpin this process remain poorly defined. Here, the authors identify TRPV2 as an essential regulator of placental development. Loss of TRPV2 disrupts trophoblast differentiation and placental architecture, leading to fetal growth restriction, impaired survival and abnormal fetal development in mice.

science.title: Pronounced megafaunal community transition driven by polymetallic nodule cover in the Northwest Pacific abyss
science.description: Polymetallic nodules provide essential hard substrata for benthic fauna and are widely assumed to enhance biodiversity on abyssal plains. Yet, our understanding of how nodule cover shapes megafaunal communities remains limited and largely restricted to low nodule cover conditions. Using a large image dataset from a nodule-rich abyssal basin in the northwest Pacific (NWP), we characterized megafaunal communities and quantitatively assessed their responses across a broad gradient of nodule cover. A total of 169 morphospecies from 14 phyla were recorded, with holothurians and sponges comprising the dominant taxa. Surprisingly, megafaunal density exhibited a U-shaped response to nodule cover, declining from low to intermediate nodule cover, remaining relatively stable at intermediate levels, and increasing sharply at high nodule cover. Community composition shifted markedly from mobile deposit-feeder dominance at low cover to sessile filter-feeder dominance at high cover. This transition was primarily driven by changes in the relative density of dominant taxa rather than species turnover. Compared with the Clarion–Clipperton Zone (CCZ), the NWP showed lower megafaunal density and distinct assemblage composition but comparable diversity, consistent with large-scale influences of particulate organic carbon flux and carbonate saturation. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized relationship between megafauna and nodule cover in the NWP nodule province and underscore the need for region-specific management of deep-sea mining. Abyssal benthic megafaunal density exhibit a unique U-shaped response to polymetallic nodule cover in the Northwest Pacific that is distinct from other well-studied areas, highlighting the need for region specific management of deep-sea mining, according to photographic surveys.

science.title: Development of biphoton entangled light spectroscopy (BELS) using Bell pairs
science.description: We introduce Biphoton Entangled Light Spectroscopy (BELS), a quantum spectroscopic technique that employs polarization-entangled Bell pairs and two-photon interference to probe material properties. In BELS, the measured signal arises not from single-photon intensities but from changes in the joint polarization and path correlations of biphoton Bell pairs transmitted through or scattered by a sample and analyzed via cross-channel coincidences. A key concept of BELS is the explicit mapping between Jones matrix operations and transformations within the Bell-state manifold. Optical elements that are equivalent under classical polarization optics can produce qualitatively distinct signatures in the coincidence landscape when interrogated with entangled photons. We demonstrate that linear birefringence and Faraday rotation generate orthogonal admixtures of Bell states, yielding experimentally distinguishable coincidence channels within a single measurement. We measure birefringence in an anisotropic dielectric and Faraday rotation in Tb3Ga5O12. By mapping the changes to the photonic entanglement, BELS establishes a new framework for future entanglement enhanced spectroscopy–a potentially powerful approach in characterizing quantum materials, nanophotonic devices, and light–matter interactions perhaps eventually at a fundamentally quantum level.

science.title: Improvement of chaotic maps for k-NN classification using Lévy-flight whale optimization: multiple dataset comparison
science.description: Metaheuristic feature selection is frequently used to improve distance-based classification on tabular datasets, yet the empirical value of adding chaotic dynamics to already enhanced optimizers remains unclear. This paper presents a controlled multi-dataset benchmark of a binary Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) feature selector combined with Lévy-flight refinement and a k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifier. Four fixed chaotic-map pairs, namely Logistic+Cubic, Sine+Sinusoidal, Singer+Circle and Iterative+Tent, are then applied to the same selected feature subspace and evaluated against the WOA+Lévy + k-NN baseline. The experiments use eight publicly available tabular datasets covering diagnostic, voting, signal-processing, combinatorial and chemical classification problems. The evaluation uses repeated stratified cross-validation, train-fold-only min-max scaling, a fixed k = 3 classifier, and non-parametric statistical testing with Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank and Holm-Bonferroni procedures. The results do not support a general claim that chaotic-map combinations improve the baseline. On the contrary, the WOA+Lévy + k-NN baseline obtains the best average rank for both accuracy and macro-F1. The Friedman test indicates a statistically detectable difference among methods for macro-F1, but the rank pattern favors the baseline, and no chaotic-map pair significantly outperforms it after Holm correction. Dataset-level analysis shows that chaotic transformations can occasionally help, as in Tic-tac-toe, but they more often degrade or leave performance unchanged, especially on Breast-cancer-wisconsin, Ionosphere, Sonar, WDBC and Wine. The contribution is therefore a reproducible boundary-condition analysis rather than a claim of a universally superior optimizer. Although the benchmark includes a raw k-NN control, a standard WOA ablation, and an EvoMapX-inspired population evolution analysis, its conclusions remain limited to the evaluated post-selection integration strategy and the four representative fixed chaotic-map pairs rather than all possible chaotic optimization designs.
